note: SNG-246 Fix D (Aevi 2026-07-27): the PLAYER-FACING receipt line per encounter kind. Today encounterReceiptForGM feeds the GM only; this is the compact mechanical block SHOWN to the player each round, sourced from the SAME receipt. Format: [icon] DEGREE · what-you-did · meter-change · finish-proximity. Tight one-liner (Erik: streamline), finish-proximity ALWAYS shown so the player sees the end coming. Tokens filled by the engine from the receipt: {degree} {actorEffect} {meterFrom} {meterTo} {meterLabel} {energyDelta} {healthDelta} {finishHint}. NOT prose - the mechanical truth beside the prose.

finishHints.near_defeat: one more solid hit ends it

fight.note: actorEffect = 'you hit for 2' / 'you miss' / 'you're staggered'. healthTaken shows only when you took damage (' · you −3 hp'). finishHint states the nearest live finish condition so a fight never ends 'the same' opaquely - the player sees WHICH road is closing.

chase.note: actorEffect = 'you gain ground' / 'you stumble'. The meter is distance, not hp - the receipt reflects the RIGHT meter per kind (that's why per-kind formats matter).

finishHints.near_bend: they're about to yield the point

standoff.note: a standoff has NO hp - the receipt shows RESOLVE moving. actorEffect = 'your point lands' / 'they counter'. This is the non-combat encounter the stationary-talker gets (SNG-237/238) - its receipt is resolve, not damage.

finishHints.near_solved: the way through is almost clear

puzzle.note: actorEffect = 'you read the mechanism' / 'the approach fails'. Insight accrues toward a solve; the receipt shows how close.

hazard.note: actorEffect = 'you find footing' / 'you slip'. A hazard is crossed, not defeated - progress meter + the cost of a bad step.

howEngineUses: Each round, the engine has the receipt (degree band, deltas, state). It picks byKind[encounterKind], fills the tokens from the receipt data, picks the finishHint whose condition is nearest-live (from the frame's finish conditions - SNG-246 §4), and renders the line BESIDE the round prose (not merged). One line, always the finish-proximity shown. Falls back to a generic 'DEGREE · meter from→to' if kind is unknown. This is the SAME receipt the GM gets, formatted for the player - the mechanical truth SHOWN, per Erik.
designNote: Per-kind formats matter because the MEALER differs (hp vs ground vs resolve vs insight vs progress) - a fight's 'foe 4→2 hp' and a standoff's 'their resolve 3→1' are both 'the meter moved', shown in the right terms. This is why a chase or standoff never reads like a mis-labeled fight. Ties SNG-230's per-kind frame.
